title: Atlassian Stock Soars 35% as Q4 Earnings Crush Estimates, Defying SaaS Slump
excerpt: The Jira and Confluence maker reported $1.77 billion in quarterly revenue, beating Wall Street forecasts by 7%, as cloud growth and AI adoption accelerate amid a broader software stock rout.
body:
• Atlassian reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.77 billion, up 28% year-over-year, beating analyst estimates of $1.66 billion
  • Adjusted earnings per share came in at $1.87, exceeding the $1.50 consensus by 25%
  • Cloud revenue surged to $1.2 billion with 31% growth, while remaining performance obligations rose 44% to $4.8 billion
  • Shares jumped 35% in extended trading, the stock's largest single-day gain in years, as the results challenge the prevailing SaaS decline narrative

Atlassian Corp. delivered a blowout fiscal fourth quarter on Thursday, sending shares surging 35% in after-hours trading and challenging the Wall Street consensus that traditional SaaS companies are in structural decline.

The Sydney-founded enterprise software maker reported revenue of $1.77 billion for the quarter ended June 30, a 28% increase from a year ago and well above the $1.66 billion consensus estimate tracked by FactSet. Adjusted earnings per share hit $1.87, crushing the $1.50 forecast.

Cloud and AI Drive the Beat

Cloud revenue — Atlassian's most closely watched metric — reached $1.2 billion, accelerating to 31% year-over-year growth. Subscription annual recurring revenue climbed to $6.6 billion, up 23%, while remaining performance obligations surged 44% to $4.8 billion, signaling strong future demand.

The company's AI offering, Rovo, has become a meaningful expansion lever. More than 80% of Fortune 500 companies now use the AI-powered teamwork tool for Jira and Confluence. Rovo-assisted actions increased more than 50% from the year-ago quarter, "translating into millions of hours saved every month for our customers," CEO and co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes wrote in a shareholder letter.

"Q4 was another outstanding quarter, capping off an incredible fiscal year. We're firing across every strategic priority — enterprise, AI and the System of Work — while driving durable, profitable growth."

— Mike Cannon-Brookes, CEO and Co-Founder, Atlassian

Record Enterprise Deals

Atlassian reported a record quarter for large enterprise contracts. The company now has more than 700 customers with annual recurring revenue exceeding $1 million. Customers in the $3 million-plus ARR tier grew over 50% from a year ago, while $5 million-plus customers grew more than 70%. The company signed the largest enterprise deal in its history with one of the world's largest consumer technology companies.

Warner Bros., Xero, and a leading AI chip manufacturer upgraded to Teamwork Collection during Q4, while Adobe and Google Cloud deepened their commitments to the Atlassian platform.

Shaking Off the SaaSpocalypse

The results land at a critical inflection point for software stocks. Over the past 18 months, the "SaaSpocalypse" — the sharp repricing of B2B software companies amid fears that AI will erode traditional seat-based business models — had punished Atlassian severely. Shares were down 32% year-to-date through Thursday's close.

The bear case was straightforward: if AI coding agents handle Jira tickets end-to-end, demand for per-seat developer tools could shrink structurally. GitHub Copilot for Jira entered public preview in March, and agentic coding tools from Cursor, Cognition, and others are already handling a rising share of pull requests at adopting companies.

Atlassian's answer is Rovo and the Teamwork Graph, a structured dataset of how teams collaborate across its products. The Q4 results suggest the strategy is gaining traction, though the structural debate over seat-based software models remains unresolved.

The company's $2.5 billion share repurchase program, authorized in October 2025, underscores management's conviction. Atlassian repurchased $1 billion in stock during the March 2026 quarter alone.

Outlook Beats Estimates, Growth Normalizes

For Q1 of fiscal 2027, Atlassian projects revenue of $1.71 billion to $1.72 billion, above the $1.66 billion analyst estimate. Cloud revenue growth is expected at about 28.5%. Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue growth is guided at approximately 13%, a deceleration from FY2026's 28% pace but reflecting tougher comparisons ahead.

The company cut 10% of its workforce — about 1,600 employees — in March as part of a restructuring toward AI and enterprise sales, a move expected to drive further margin improvement alongside the revenue growth.

Founded in 2002 by Cannon-Brookes and Scott Farquhar with $10,000 on a credit card, Atlassian has grown into a global platform with more than 350,000 customers. The company maintains a significant engineering presence in India, with major offices in Bangalore, and its tools are a staple for Indian tech professionals across Silicon Valley and global technology hubs.
